page: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g-480s is a general-purpose virtual server within the VX1 Cloud Compute series. The instance is built with 8 dedicated vCPUs running on 4 physical AMD EPYC cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core. It is configured with 32 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory distribution. Local storage is directly bundled as a 480 GB NVMe SSD. Networking configuration includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, and the server does not feature GPU accelerators. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as VAES and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions.

Performance benchmarks show pronounced strengths in single-threaded throughput. Single-core stress-ng evaluations and gzip compression test results place the instance in the top tier of comparable systems, alongside high single-threaded text processing scores. Conversely, multi-threaded compute metrics—such as Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core—fall within the median 50% band, bounded by the 4-physical-core count. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 71.66 GB/s, while write bandwidth sustains 41.2 GB/s. For machine learning tasks, prompt processing on 7B models shows weaker performance falling in the lower 25%, while small 135M model generation rates in the top decile.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, dedicated vCPU scheduling ensures predictable computational throughput without resource contention from neighbor instances. The pairing of dedicated compute with bundled NVMe storage provides consistent I/O and CPU delivery. This profile makes the instance appropriate for production web serving, relational databases, in-memory caching with Redis, CI/CD runners, and general back-end microservices.

It includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without GPU acceleration. CPU benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compute, high-speed gzip compression, and strong text processing, enabled by modern instructions like AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16. Multi-core compute benchmarks, uncached memory bandwidth (71.66 GB/s read), and Redis throughput remain within median percentiles, while heavier LLM prompt processing shows lower efficiency. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and dedicated hardware resource allocation provide steady, predictable operational capacity. The server fits production workloads such as web serving, relational databases, Redis caching layers, and automated build pipelines.
